title: Paychecks on the 1st and 15th
subtitle: Valerie's paycheck shows on the calendar on the 1st and the 15th, and on the Friday before when either day falls on a weekend.
intro: The code is already in your Sheet. The upgrade adds one column, **Paydays (days of month)**, at the far right of the **Expected Income** tab.

**What does not change:** your transactions, the Income tab, and the Monthly Plan. The plan still counts two paychecks a month for Valerie. Only the calendar moves her paydays to the days the money actually lands.

steps.text: In the Sheet, open **File → Version history → Name current version** and name it `Before paydays 2026-11-25`.
Reload the Sheet. Open the **App Setup** tab and check that **Build Script Version** reads `1.34.0`. If it shows an older number, wait a minute and reload again.
Open **Finance Tracker → Upgrade workbook (keeps data)** and confirm.
steps.done: The report finishes without errors. On **Expected Income**, the last column is **Paydays (days of month)**, and it is empty.

steps.text: Tell Claude the upgrade is done.
steps.done: Claude sets Valerie's paycheck to **Semimonthly** with Paydays `1, 15`.

steps.text: Open **Finance Tracker → 📅 Calendar** and click **Whole month** for December.
steps.done: Valerie's paycheck shows on **Tuesday, December 1** and **Tuesday, December 15**.
Valerie's paycheck shows on **Friday, November 13** (the 15th is a Sunday). Her November 1st paycheck came on Friday, October 30, so it is in October, not November.
